The acrostolion is the tip of the stolos, and stolos is the name for the timber that projects from the ptyche and extends to the prow; ptyche is the name for the place where the ship's name is inscribed. Therefore the acrostolion at the prow is not the aphlaston, but the poet applies the term to the stern when he says (O 716 sq.):
